text:
mike: Hey folks, first day . Trying to get dev env working on an M2 Mac (Fish shell) and a small Ubuntu VM. I followed the quickstart but hit a few weird things: asdf doesn't seem to initialize in fish, ruby gems fail linking to openssl, and repo scripts expect REDWOOD_API_KEY/KUBECONFIG but i prefer fish-style envs. Any fish-specific tips or a short minimal checklist?

rachel: welcome! Few notes for Fish + asdf + macOS M1/M2: 1) asdf needs a tiny different init for fish (or use the asdf-fish plugin). Add to config.fish:
`source (brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.fish`
or if you cloned asdf: `source $HOME/.asdf/asdf.fish`
2) brew install openssl@3 pkg-config direnv corepack
3) export OpenSSL flags before building Ruby/gems: in Fish syntax:
`set -x LDFLAGS "-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib"`
`set -x CPPFLAGS "-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include"`
`set -x PKG_CONFIG_PATH "/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig"`
Then `asdf install ruby <version>`; re-run gem installs after that.

rachel: extras: run `brew install rustup-init` then `rustup-init` if a package errors about cargo. For Node we prefer corepack + pnpm: `corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@8 --activate`. Avoid mixing nvm.

rachel: secrets + fish: we use direnv. Create a fish-style env file (not committed) e.g. `~/.config/redwood/env.fish` with fish exports:
`set -x REDWOOD_API_KEY sk-local-...`
`set -x KUBECONFIG $HOME/.kube/config-redwood`
Then in the repo `.envrc` call `source_env ~/.config/redwood/env.fish` (direnv supports fish). If you use sops/age for encrypted files, store the key in your mac keychain or use the company vault. Do not commit plaintext.

shell-bot: quick checklist (auto): brew, asdf, direnv, rustup, corepack/pnpm, set fish export flags for openssl, add ssh ed25519 to GitHub.

mike: thanks rachel. one edge: asdf node plugin tried to gpg-verify node tarball and failed (no gpg). on fish should i `brew install gnupg` and run the plugin import?

rachel: yep install gnupg via brew and run the plugin's key import: `~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`. If that errors, the plugin README includes manual key URLs.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-5321 to grant mike repo access and provision a dev kubecontext.

mike: perfect, i'll try the fish init + openssl flags + rustup and report back if anything still breaks :thumbsup:
